member.name: T:Microsoft.Internal.Windows.Tools.Build.Utilities.EventSourceRootedActivity
member.summary: Provides support for EventSource activities.

remarks.para: An activity consists of one Start event, any number of normal events, and one Stop event. All events written by EventSourceRootedActivity (Start, normal, and Stop) are tagged with a unique activity ID (a GUID). In addition, the Start event can optionally include the ID of a related (parent) activity, making it possible to track activity nesting.

This class inherits from IDisposable to enable its use in using blocks, not because it owns any unmanaged resources. It is not necessarily an error to abandon an activity without calling Dispose. Calling Dispose() on an activity in the "Started" state is equivalent to calling Stop("Dispose"). Calling Dispose() on an activity in any other state is a no-op.
This class adheres to Engineering Systems-specific requirements for propagating activity root information through the activity ID tree, thus the class name 'EventSource*Rooted*Activity'.

Notable differences from the general-purpose EventSourceActivity class provided in Windows sources:
The public constructor forces 'chaining' of activities off a parent activity. Only the outer-most layer (OptionsParser) should create a top-level activity.
Events must be logged through the activity instance (the contained EventSource instance is no longer exposed) to encourage activity-associated events.

member.name: T:Microsoft.Internal.Windows.Tools.Build.Utilities.OptionsParser
member.summary:
An abstract class that Build Tool programs should subclass in order to get consistent command line parsing behavior and error reporting.
The subclass defines public properties that are automatically made into command line options of the same name. Optional options require a DefaultValue attribute to specify their value when not given.
Arguments are of the form /Name=Value or -Name:Value which matches Powershell syntax relatively closely. The -Name:Value is generally better for compatibility through CMD as CMD converts "=" to " " and can interpret some "/options" incorrectly.
Arguments values will have environment variables expanded when given in %name% format. This allows calling these tools without first running within CMD.exe to expand environment variables.
Argument validation is available via the DataAnnotations.Validation attributes. Any/all such validations are supported.
An argument of @filename will read the given file and interpret each line in that file as another argument to parse, just like response files. @filename can be combined with other command line options and can be nested within a response file too. Again, environment variables are expanded, even for @%name% syntax such that you can use the environment variables to form path names to response files.
This is built with no mutable static types such that commands can be joined into a single binary for execution in addition to running stand-alone binaries.
All arguments must be prefixed with an option - thus there are no positional arguments. This is mainly to provide strong fidelity of expression and less chance of mistaken intent.
Instances of these commands can be easily used as either native command .EXE tools or as libraries that are called from a managed environment. The unit tests show the second form.

member.summary: Dump a response-file compatible argument list of the options
member.remarks:
This will take all properties and dump them as a stream that is in the format of a response file that can be used by this parser. This includes all options and their values, including any default values. The values are all after expanding any environment variables. This way it can be used as an audit of what the options effectively were when combinded with the current defaults and those that came from the command line.
Options are ordered by their name and array options have their array in the order that was given such that replaying the response file will reproduce the exact same state within the object.
The one option that is not dumped is the "DumpArguments" option as that is the option that would trigger this behavior.
